privacy.contact: For privacy questions, contact Frank Zhu through the linked GitHub issue tracker. Google may process Play Store, device-backup, and crash information under its own privacy settings and policies.
privacy.retention: Local data remains until it is replaced or you uninstall the app or clear its storage in Android Settings. Backups and copies you have shared must be managed separately with their respective services. The developer holds no server copy of your games or settings.
privacy.sharing: When you choose Share, the game record is passed to the recipient or service you select. Opening source-code or support links takes you to GitHub, which applies its own privacy policy. Information you submit in a GitHub issue may be public; avoid including private information.
privacy.storage: Saved games, learning progress, and settings stay in the app’s storage on your device. The bundled computer engine processes positions locally. Your operating system may include app data in device backups according to your backup settings.
privacy.summary: Xiangqi is developed by Frank Zhu. The app works offline and does not collect or transmit personal data to the developer. It has no accounts, advertising, tracking, analytics, or automatic diagnostic uploads.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
rules.advisor: Moves one point diagonally inside the palace.
rules.cannon: Moves like a chariot, but captures by jumping exactly one intervening piece.
rules.chariot: Moves any distance along a clear file or rank.
rules.elephant: Moves two points diagonally, cannot jump, and cannot cross the river.
rules.general: Moves one point orthogonally inside the palace. The generals may not face on an open file.
rules.goal: Checkmate the opposing general. Red moves first. A side with no legal move loses.
rules.horse: Moves one orthogonal step then one diagonal step; the first step cannot be blocked.
rules.notation: Files are a–i and ranks are 0–9. A move such as b2e2 records its source and destination. The game stores the starting FEN plus this ordered move list for reliable replay and sharing.
rules.soldier: Moves forward one point. After crossing the river it may also move sideways, never backward.
rules.title: Rules
settings.engineNote: Computer play uses the bundled Pikafish engine and NNUE network entirely on-device. No account or network access is required.
settings.rulesPolicyExplanation: New games use Pikafish’s rules for repetition, perpetual checking and chasing, the 60-move rule, and insufficient material. Perpetual checking or chasing can result in a loss rather than a draw. Earlier saved games keep their recorded rules.
